record.subgoal: Prove that left cosets of a subgroup H in a finite group G partition G.
record.attempt_summary: For any x in G, x lies in xH because e in H. If aH and bH intersect, choose ah1=bh2; then b^{-1}a=h2h1^{-1} in H, which implies aH=bH. Hence distinct left cosets are disjoint and cover G.
adapted_from: Standard coset proof pattern from Lagrange theorem background

record.subgoal: Prove that every left coset gH has cardinality |H| via the bijection h -> gh.
record.attempt_summary: For fixed g in G, the map H -> gH given by h -> gh is surjective by definition and injective by left cancellation in the group. Therefore |gH|=|H|.
adapted_from: Standard coset proof pattern from Lagrange theorem background

record.attempt_summary: Because the finite group G is partitioned into [G:H] disjoint left cosets and every coset has |H| elements, summing over the partition gives |G|=[G:H]|H|. The index is an integer, so |H| divides |G|.

record.subgoal: Choose a nonidentity a in G of prime order-size p and apply the divisibility result to H=<a> to get |<a>|=p and hence G=<a>.
record.attempt_summary: Since |G|=p with p prime, G has a nonidentity element a. The subgroup <a> contains e and a, so its order is greater than 1. Lagrange gives |<a>| divides p. The only positive divisors of p are 1 and p, so |<a>|=p. As <a> is a subset of G with the same finite cardinality as G, <a>=G; hence G is cyclic.
used_results: Lagrange lemma proved in the same blueprint
adapted_from: Target-theorem standard route from search background

record.subgoal: Use Cauchy's theorem to obtain an element of order p and conclude cyclicity.
record.attempt_summary: The plan would close immediately if Cauchy's theorem were admitted. However, proving Cauchy's theorem is a stronger obligation than this target and importing it from an external paper would require unnecessary citation and paper-proof checking. The Lagrange route already solves the problem self-containedly.
key_stuck_points: Cauchy's theorem is stronger than needed and would introduce an avoidable dependency.
migration_failures: The theorem-search result is applicable but oversized for the target; relying on it would violate the intent to avoid black-box external results when a direct elementary proof is available.
